result.topic_en: Formula-only calculations: the left half transforms a Laplace-type equation $\Delta u + \frac14 u = 0$ into new coordinates and solves it by series and definite integrals, and the right half estimates integrals of the form $\int \frac{\sin hp}{\sin p} f(p)\,dp$ (Dirichlet-kernel limits) with inequalities on alternating partial sums, plus cross-ratio substitutions for an integral of the form $\int (y-a)^\alpha (y-b)^\beta \dots$.

methods.what: Substitution $u=r^{-1/2}v$ reducing the 4D Laplace equation in cylindrical-type coordinates to $\Delta v+\frac{1}{r^2}(v_{\psi\psi}+\frac14 v)=0$
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial r^2}+\frac{1}{rr}\left(\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial\psi^2}+\frac14 v\right)=0$

Series solution (Bessel-type) and its integral representation
Recurrence for the coefficients of a power-series solution
Beta-integral representation of a ratio of Pi (Gamma) functions
Upper and lower bounds on an alternating sum of the integral pieces
Cross-ratio substitution mapping the branch points a, b, c to 0, ∞, 1 for $\int\prod(y-a)^\alpha\dots$ with exponents summing to −2
